---
title: "Wave-1 cutover packets: Calendar, Mail, Apps, Meet, Roadmap"
description: "Per-app Worker identity, routes, bindings, build command, Vercel rollback target and smoke commands for the wave-1 Cloudflare cutover."
updatedAt: "2026-11-09"
audience: developers
---

Each packet is what the release operator needs to flip one app from Vercel to its
native Cloudflare Worker, and to flip it back. Provider writes (DNS, routes,
custom domains, aliases, deployments) stay with the release operator; the source
only produces the sealed Worker bytes. Secret values never appear here, only names.

## Common

- Build (CI parity): `bun turbo:local run build --filter=@tuturuuu/<app> --concurrency=2`, then
  `node scripts/ci/wave1-native-artifact.mjs prepare <app> production <sha> <workers-subdomain>`,
  `node scripts/ci/wave1-native-runtime.mjs <app> production <sha>` (needs `CI=true`) and
  `node scripts/ci/wave1-native-publish.mjs dry-run <app> production <sha>`.
- The production publication profile (`scripts/ci/wave1-native-profiles.json`) uploads a
  route-free Worker (`workers_dev: false`, `routes: []`). Binding the canonical host is a
  separate provider step, so uploading never moves traffic.
- Production publication is gated by `productionPublicationPolicy` in `tuturuuu.ci.ts`
  and the `wave1-native-production.yaml` dispatch, which currently lists `calendar` only.
  Admitting `mail` or `apps` needs the same reviewed cutover PR plus the workflow option and
  its protected environment.
- Rollback: Vercel can no longer redeploy `calendar` or `mail` from `main`. Their build
  command now emits a native Worker and Vercel fails with `NEXT_OUTPUT_DIR_MISSING`, so the
  rollback target is the retained READY deployment below, restored by moving the alias.
  Never delete these deployments until a full release cycle has run on the Worker.
- Smoke, after the flip, per host `<host>`:

  ```sh
  curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://<host>/            # expect 200 or the login redirect 307, never 5xx
  curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://<host>/login | head -1             # expect 200 or 307 to tuturuuu.com/login
  curl -sS https://<host>/api/build-info                                # expect the exact source sha and runtime native
  ```

  A passing smoke shows `server: cloudflare` and no `x-vercel-id` header.

## Verified at `506c1ea9`

The full production-profile sequence (build, seal, original-bytes workerd acceptance,
upload-limit dry-run, final seal) passes on an isolated checkout for these apps:

| App | Script bytes | Gzip bytes | Modules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Calendar | 23181018 | 3315032 | 221 |
| Mail | 6123439 | 1958325 | 103 |
| Apps | 2355083 | 567748 | 25 |

Every size is inside the recorded paid-plan limits (64 MiB script). Mail and Apps runtime
acceptance returns `200` for `GET`/`HEAD /api/build-info`, `405` for `POST`, and `307` for the
unauthenticated workspace route. Meet and Roadmap use their own workflows and are covered above.

## Meet

`meet.tuturuuu.com` is already served by the `tuturuuu-meet` Worker (`server: cloudflare`,
anonymous `/` answers 307 to the Web login). Source carries the custom-domain route in
`apps/meet/void.config.ts`. Bindings: `ASSETS`, `WORKER_SELF_REFERENCE`, `ABUSE_GUARD`
(service `tuturuuu-abuse-guard`), R2 cache bucket `tuturuuu-meet-cache`,
`IMAGES`, and the `MEET_LIVE` Durable Object (migration tag `meet-live-v1`). Required secret
names: `MEET_REALTIME_TOKEN_SECRET`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`.
Meet is not part of the wave-1 profile set: `meet-cloudflare.yaml` validates it on every
change (native build, emitted-config receipt, restored-artifact acceptance) and its `deploy`
job publishes from the `production` ref with a deployment marker. Meet AI stays contained (`MEET_AI_DISABLED=true`). Migration changes follow the Meet
migration serialization and are not part of this packet. Vercel holds no READY production
deployment for Meet (all recent ones are canceled), so rollback for a Meet regression is the
previous Worker version, not Vercel.

## Roadmap

`tuturuuu.com/roadmap` is served by the `tuturuuu-roadmap` Worker through Web's proxy
(`apps/web/src/lib/roadmap-public-proxy.ts`), which fetches the non-redirecting worker origin
and never forwards cookies or authorization. The Worker also owns the routes
`tuturuuu.com/roadmap` and `tuturuuu.com/roadmap/*` in `apps/roadmap/void.config.ts`.

- Rollback: remove the `isRoadmapPublicPath` branch in `proxy.ts` (Web then serves its own page)
  or point `ROADMAP_UPSTREAM_ORIGIN` elsewhere; no Worker deletion is needed.
- Smoke: `curl -sS -L --max-redirs 3 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://tuturuuu.com/roadmap`
  expects `200`; `https://tuturuuu.com/vi/roadmap` expects one redirect to `/roadmap`.
